mechanism: There is no descriptor-level warnings channel anywhere in the tree. %PARSE-MINISCRIPT-DESCRIPTOR (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:889-922) builds the node and runs %CHECK-MINISCRIPT-SANE; it performs no node walk for unsafe timelocks, and the OUT-DESC struct (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:589) has no warnings slot at all -- its slots are KIND KEYS THRESHOLD SUB TREE SCRIPT ADDRESS NODE XONLY-SCRIPT-P. %PROCESS-DESCRIPTOR-IMPORT (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2156-2280) does keep a warnings list, but only three strings are ever pushed into it: 'Range not given, using default keypool range' (:2212), 'Not all private keys provided. Some wallet functionality may return unexpected errors' (:2258) and 'Unknown output type, cannot set descriptor to active.' (:2274). Core's MiniscriptDescriptor constructor walks the node with ForEachNode and, for every OLDER fragment whose value part (k with SEQUENCE_LOCKTIME_TYPE_FLAG masked off) exceeds SEQUENCE_LOCKTIME_MASK = 65535, records 'height-based relative locktime: older(N) > 65535 blocks is unsafe' or the 'time-based ... > (65535 * 512) seconds is unsafe' variant (refs/bitcoin/src/script/descriptor.cpp:1648-1661); DescriptorImpl::Warnings aggregates a descriptor's own warnings with its sub-descriptors' (descriptor.cpp:1041-1048), which is what carries a miniscript node's warning out through the enclosing wsh(); and ProcessDescriptorImport copies them into the importdescriptors result (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/rpc/backup.cpp:243-245), the only production consumer of Warnings() in Core.
consequence: BIP68 carries only 16 bits of relative-locktime value, so older(100000) is enforced as 100000 & 0xFFFF = 34464 blocks -- about a third of the lock the operator wrote. Core tells them at import time; we accept it silently. There is no consensus split and no spendability problem: our script generation and ms-check-older (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:163-190, Core's CheckSequence) both agree with consensus about what the script actually enforces, so the coins behave identically on both implementations. The whole loss is the report, which makes this a bounded reporting divergence -- S3. The realistic harm is an operator setting up a recovery path they believe is roughly two years and getting roughly eight months, with nothing in the importdescriptors result to contradict them.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-miniscript-s3, warm image, probes build/ga11probe/p5.lisp and build/ga11probe/p6.lisp (git-ignored), each run twice with identical results. p5 drives parse-descriptor with :require-checksum t on :testnet4 over Core's own descriptor_older_warnings vectors (refs/bitcoin/src/test/descriptor_tests.cpp:1291-1336): wsh(and_v(v:pk(0379e45b..),older(65535))) accepted; older(65536) accepted; older(4259840) (= 65536 | SEQUENCE_LOCKTIME_TYPE_FLAG, Core's time-based case) accepted; after(1000000) accepted; older(100000) accepted. Core expects zero warnings for the first and fourth and exactly one warning each for the second and third; we produce no warning for any of them, and there is nowhere for one to go -- the out-desc slot list read back from the image is (KIND KEYS THRESHOLD SUB TREE SCRIPT ADDRESS NODE XONLY-SCRIPT-P), with no warnings slot. p6 then executes the shipped RPC end to end: a regtest wallet-chain node (tests/support/wallet.lisp with-wallet-chain-node), createwallet 'wo' with private keys disabled, then rpc-importdescriptors of each descriptor above with timestamp 'now'. All four returned exactly (("success" . T)) -- no warnings array on older(65536), older(100000) or older(4259840). Core side read at d3056bc: descriptor.cpp:1648-1661, descriptor.cpp:1041-1048, wallet/rpc/backup.cpp:243-245, and a tree-wide grep confirming backup.cpp:243 is the only production caller of Warnings(). Ours: src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:589 (the struct), :889-922 (the miniscript descriptor parser), src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2212, :2258, :2274 (the only three warning strings).
fix_shape: Give the parsed descriptor a warnings channel and fill it the way Core does. Add a WARNINGS slot to OUT-DESC (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:589) and an accessor that aggregates a descriptor's own warnings with those of %OUT-DESC-CHILDREN, mirroring DescriptorImpl::Warnings (descriptor.cpp:1041-1048) -- the recursion is what makes a warning raised on the miniscript node visible through the enclosing wsh() or tr(). In %PARSE-MINISCRIPT-DESCRIPTOR (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:889-922), after %CHECK-MINISCRIPT-SANE, walk the node once and for every :OLDER fragment compute value-part = (logandc2 k +sequence-locktime-type-flag+); when it exceeds 65535, push Core's exact string -- 'height-based relative locktime: older(~D) > 65535 blocks is unsafe' or 'time-based relative locktime: older(~D) > (65535 * 512) seconds is unsafe', chosen by whether the type flag is set in the RAW k, and formatted with the RAW k, not the masked value. Then in %PROCESS-DESCRIPTOR-IMPORT (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2156-2280) append the parsed descriptor's warnings to the existing warnings list before %PUSH-WARNINGS, at the point Core does (backup.cpp:243-245, right after the expansion check). Do not warn on :AFTER -- Core's 'no false positive for absolute timelocks' case (descriptor_tests.cpp:1327-1335) is a required negative control -- and keep older(65535) warning-free, since the boundary is strictly greater than. Test with all four of Core's vectors through importdescriptors, asserting both the presence and the absence of the warnings array.
